headline: Samsung TVs record audio & screenshots for targeted ads, bounty hunter finds
summary: A cybersecurity researcher uncovered extensive privacy breaches in Tizen OS, including detailed user telemetry and cross-device identification, even using connected soundbars as microphones.
details: Cybersecurity bounty hunter log4j discovered what they termed "PRIVACY HORROR" on their 2025 Samsung TV after noticing unusually targeted ads. Their investigation involved reverse-engineering the TV's Tizen OS.

The researcher found concerning code revealing detailed user telemetry from packet logging, audio categorization, and screenshots. It also included cross-device identification for ad tracking, all designed to extract user information for targeted advertising.

Log4j theorizes that the sluggish performance of Samsung TVs may stem from extensive post-processing of user data. This includes computer vision, audio analysis, and AI models tracking viewing habits, skipped ads, and video progress.

A particularly alarming finding was the TV's ability to utilize connected devices with microphones, such as soundbars or Bluetooth devices, to record audio, even if the TV itself lacks a built-in mic.

Hugging Face engineer ngxson partially corroborated the microphone behavior on a rooted Tizen TV, observing a 5-second microphone activation. However, their modified TV setup means an unmodified device might behave differently.
Log4j reported being banned by OpenAI for "cyber abuse" after using their tools for local reverse engineering, despite arguing they did not violate terms of use or exploit vulnerabilities.

Samsung is not alone; other brands like LG have faced similar accusations of customer surveillance. Log4j is currently preparing a comprehensive write-up of their findings, including methods for others to investigate.

headline_marked: [[Gemini's Scheduled actions simplify everyday routines]] in 5 key ways, boosting productivity
headline: Gemini's Scheduled actions simplify everyday routines in 5 key ways, boosting productivity
summary: Instead of repetitive manual tasks, Gemini can now run prompts regularly, delivering personalized results directly to you, from daily plans to news digests.
details: Gemini's Scheduled actions feature allows users to automate repetitive tasks by scheduling prompts to run regularly. This eliminates the need to manually open the app and ask the same questions daily or weekly, with results waiting for the user.

Users can create scheduled actions directly on the Gemini website by navigating to the "Scheduled" sidebar. Here, they can describe the task, set a frequency, and save it. Gemini also offers suggested schedules for common tasks like news digests or financial trend tracking.

One practical application is daily planning. Gemini can be scheduled to review calendars, important unread emails, and to-do lists every evening. It then highlights upcoming deadlines and suggests the top three priorities for the next day, requiring connection to Google Workspace.

Another use case is staying informed with a personalized news digest. Users can ask Gemini to prepare a roundup of important developments in specific subjects, such as Android updates or AI, at a set time. The digest includes summaries and source links, with notifications sent upon completion.

Gemini's scheduled actions can also facilitate structured learning. Users can set up a schedule to learn new concepts at their own pace, starting with basics and gradually moving to advanced topics. This includes subjects like self-hosting, with each lesson ending with questions to test understanding.
